additional_info.subject: RE: ID0395279 - DC/Si-D/FI - [MP / R2 170001449] - Unable to charge with either outlet CRM:00641000877
additional_info.body:
Dear Harjunpaa Sakari,
I hope this message finds you well.
Regarding the reported issue, we analyzed the logs and observed some anomalies during the analysis. Specifically, we identified the following error:
"Error polling coap://10.20.17.100:5683/state Error: No reply in 4.25s."
This indicates that the SECC is unable to communicate with the controller.
Based on our findings, we recommend the following steps to address the issue. As an initial step, try rebooting the SECC.
Additionally, verify all wirings and connections as per the schematics, and replace the Ethernet cable if necessary. If the issue persists after performing these steps, we suggest proceeding with replacing the SECC2300.and keep in mind that please carry the spare of SECC 2300 and ethernet cable in case replacement is needed.
Kindly refer the below AWS logs where we can see error:
"Error polling coap://10.20.17.100:5683/state Error: No reply in 4.25s.
Upon reviewing the logs on SCB, I've detected anomalies related to the CableTempSensor error of the DC1 cable. This error has recurred 2 times since week. Therefore, we suggest examining the cable temperature sensor of outlet DC1 and, if necessary, replacing the cable.
Kindly refer mentioned steps to be followed to trouble shoot the fault which is leading to this error flags.
Step 1:
Turn off the power supply to the charger.
Step 2:
Identify the cables P1, P2, N1 & N2 associated to Pt1000 refer below picture for your ref.
Step 3:
Check the ambient temperature and note it, then using multimeter measure the resistance of P1, P2, N1 & N2.
Step 4: Click on the following link to see the resistance table of Pt 1000 pertaining to the temperature and its corresponding resistance.
https://www.sterlingsensors.co.uk/pt1000-resistance-table
Kindly refer the below knowledge article to check the cable sensor,
Knowledge Article: Knowledge Article for ISP: Emobility_SICD_HW_DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101 and EVSE_TempLowerLimit_ low temperature - Dynamics 365
,,
Note-; Additionally, we noticed that the charger firmware is old. To mitigate the errors you’ve encountered, we strongly recommend upgrading your charger’s firmware. Firmware updates often include bug fixes, performance enhancements, and improved compatibility with electric vehicle communication protocols, ensuring better system stability and functionality. (First recommendation to upgrade the charger with latest firmware version)
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav Malokar
